s2.p1: Glasgow was a dance-hall city: the **Plaza** opened in 1922, the **Locarno** in 1926. **Dancesport Scotland** was set up in 1945.
s2.p2: WDSF expelled it in 2022, along with its Welsh counterpart. Since 2024, the UK’s full WDSF member is the **British DanceSport Federation**.

s3.p: during World War II, the peak of a **golden age** of social dancing that ran from 1914 to the mid-1950s, when rock ’n’ roll won over the young.

s4.p1: From **Hamilton**, he joined a dance school in Glasgow’s Gorbals. With **Gaynor Fairweather**, he won ==14 world Latin titles==, 13 of them in a row.
s4.p2: A Guinness World Record. Appointed MBE in 1991, he has been **president of the World Dance Council** since 2005.

s5.name: HIGHLAND
s5.p: Solo, precise footwork, mostly to the **bagpipes**: the Fling, the Sword Dance. Once danced only by men, today about **95% of dancers** are female.

s5.name: CEILIDH
s5.p: A caller teaches each dance on the spot: **Strip the Willow**, the Gay Gordons, the Eightsome Reel. Fiddle and accordion, at weddings, Hogmanay and Burns Night.

s6.p: After **Culloden**, a 1746 law banned Highland dress, soldiers aside. The Seann Triubhas, ‘old trousers’, is said to celebrate the kilt’s return.

s7.p: In Stirling, the **Scottish Official Board of Highland Dancing**. In Edinburgh, the International Council of Ballroom Dancing, today the **World Dance Council**.
s7.p2: A dancer from **Scone** wins the junior World Highland Dancing title: ==the only Scottish winner== of the three world crowns.

DanceSport Scotland (DSS) and DanceSport Wales (DSW) listed under NMB expelled, 7 May 2022
British DanceSport Federation: full WDSF member for the United Kingdom since 25 October 2024
Burns and Fairweather: 14 World Latin titles, 13 consecutive World Professional Latin titles; Guinness World Record
Donnie Burns from Hamilton, joined a dance school in Glasgow's Gorbals
Donnie Burns: Scottish, 14-time World Professional Latin champion, MBE 1991 Birthday Honours, WDC President since 2005
Donnie Burns MBE signs as WDC President; WDC established 22 September 1950 in Edinburgh as ICBD
ICBD founded during a dance congress in Edinburgh, 22 September 1950
Scottish Official Board of Highland Dancing formed 15 January 1950 in Stirling; Highland dancing mainly solo, bagpipes most common, Fling, Sword Dance
RSOBHD formed in 1950 as the World Governing Body for Highland Dancing
Highland Fling: no clear evidence before the late 18th century; competitions at Highland Games
Highland dancing moved from an exclusively male pursuit to more than 95% female dancers; Seann Triubhas means 'old trousers', celebrates return of the kilt after the ban ended in 1782
Ceilidh from Gaelic for 'visit'; caller; Strip the Willow, Gay Gordons, Eightsome Reel; fiddle and accordion; weddings, Burns Night, Hogmanay
Ceilidh etymology (Old Irish cele, Gaelic 'visit'); ceilidh bands common at weddings in 2020s Scotland
Dress Act 1746 (royal assent 12 Aug 1746, after Culloden) banned Highland dress, soldiers exempt; repealed 1 July 1782
Glasgow had 256 venues licensed for public dancing in the 1930s (corroborates scale of the dance-hall scene)
Donnie Burns born in Hamilton; 14 WDC World Pro Latin titles (13 consecutive 1984-1996, plus 1998); MBE 1991; WDC president since 2005, still in post July 2026
Highland dancing originally performed only by men; today competitions about 95% female
